title: Cardinal bound for all small simplicial diagrams and their cones
statement: Use simplicial sets, simplicial maps, degreewise coproducts and right join cones $A^{\triangleright}=A\star\Delta^0$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and smallness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]: $\rho$-small means fewer than $\rho$ nondegenerate simplices. Let $\lambda<\kappa$ be infinite regular cardinals, with $\kappa$ uncountable and $\mu^\nu<\kappa$ for all $\mu<\kappa$ and $\nu<\lambda$. Let $V$ be a set of cardinality less than $\kappa$, and let $(B_v)_{v\in V}$ be a family of $\kappa$-small simplicial sets. Consider triples $(v,A,\phi)$ with $A$ $\lambda$-small and $\phi:A\to B_v$ a simplicial map. An isomorphism of triples fixes $v$ and is a simplicial isomorphism $h:A\to A'$ with $\phi' h=\phi$. There exists a set $R$ of representatives of these isomorphism classes with $|R|<\kappa$. Both degreewise coproducts $\coprod_{r\in R}A_r$ and $\coprod_{r\in R}A_r^{\triangleright}$ are $\kappa$-small. Empty shapes, empty $V$, and $\lambda=\aleph_0$ are included.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.4.4.2, successor-stage set S on printed p. 433, using the sharp cardinal inequality of Section 5.4.2; cardinal estimate expanded from the returned Step 4. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial or quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Write $N(B_v)$ for all nondegenerate simplices of $B_v$, in all degrees, with the degree retained. By the smallness convention in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], each has size less than $\kappa$. Put $W=\coprod_{v\in V}N(B_v)$. Regularity of $\kappa$ means that a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets, each of size less than $\kappa$, still has size less than $\kappa$; hence $|W|<\kappa$. Let $T=\coprod_{v\in V,n\geq0}(B_v)_n$, retaining both tags. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], an element of $T$ is specified uniquely by its tagged nondegenerate ancestor and its surjective finite ordinal map. Encode that map by the natural number $n$ and its finite list of values. These data inject $T$ into finite lists on $\mathbf N\amalg W$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-list-cardinality] gives $|T|\leq\max(\aleph_0,|\mathbf N\amalg W|)<\kappa$, using uncountability and regularity of $\kappa$.

proof.text:
Fix a cardinal $
u<\lambda$, and label the nondegenerate simplices of a shape $A$ bijectively by the initial ordinal $I=
u$; write them $a_i$ of dimension $d_i$. For every $i$ record $d_i$ and, for every injective ordinal map $\delta:[m]\hookrightarrow[d_i]$ (including the identity), the unique expression $A(\delta)(a_i)=A(\eta)(a_j)$ with $\eta:[m]	woheadrightarrow[d_j]$ furnished by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. There are only finitely many such injections into a fixed $[d_i]$: each is determined by its nonempty image subset. Order these injections by the finite lists of their values. Each record is a finite list of natural numbers and labels in $I$, using lengths as delimiters. Finally record the tagged simplex $\phi(a_i)\in T$. This produces one finite word $c_i$ on the disjoint alphabet $X_
u=\mathbf N\amalg I\amalg T$ per label. The records contain actual target simplices, which may be degenerate; no nondegeneracy of $\phi(a_i)$ is assumed.

proof.text: The records determine the triple up to the required isomorphism. Indeed, [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] identifies $A_n$ with the pairs $(i,\sigma)$ where $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[d_i]$, by $(i,\sigma)\mapsto A(\sigma)(a_i)$. For $\alpha:[p]\to[n]$, factor $\sigma\alpha=\delta\tau$ by listing its image in increasing order, with $\tau:[p]\twoheadrightarrow[m]$ and $\delta:[m]\hookrightarrow[d_i]$. If the recorded entry for $(i,\delta)$ is $(j,\eta)$, then $A(\alpha)$ sends $(i,\sigma)$ to $(j,\eta\tau)$, directly by functoriality. Thus identical records give degreewise bijections commuting with every simplicial operator. Moreover $\phi(i,\sigma)=B_v(\sigma)(\phi(a_i))$, so the same bijections commute with the maps to $B_v$. This proves the assertion for each fixed $v$. It also constructs a canonical set-sized model for every realized record, on these pairs, with exactly the displayed operators and map; the simplicial identities hold because the formula agrees with a realization. No selection from a proper class of shapes is needed.

For a fixed $(v,

u|)<\kappa$, since $
u<\lambda<\kappa$ and Step 1 bounds $T$. By the stated exponent hypothesis there are at most $\mu_
u^
u<\kappa$ such records. Restricting to realized records cannot increase this bound. The collection of cardinals $
u<\lambda$ is a set of size at most $\lambda<\kappa$ (represent each by its initial ordinal below $\lambda$). Take the union of the realized canonical models of Step 3 over these $
u$ and over $v\in V$. Two applications of regularity give a set of models of cardinality less than $\kappa$. Every triple occurs up to isomorphism in that set. Quotient this set by the stipulated isomorphism relation and choose one element per class, giving the desired set $R$ with $|R|<\kappa$.

proof.text:
For $
u=0$ the record is the unique empty function and its model is the empty simplicial set, with the unique map to each fixed $B_v$. If $V=\varnothing$, the resulting model set and $R$ are empty. For $\lambda=\aleph_0$, each $
u<\lambda$ is finite: each generator has a finite record even when its dimension is large. The estimate uses $\mu_
u^
u$, never $\mu_
u^{\aleph_0}$, so it imposes no continuum bound absent from the hypotheses. Empty targets cause no exception: no nonempty source has a simplicial map to the empty target, and such records are simply not realized.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.2, printed p. 433: the cardinal estimate for the successor-stage representative set S and its cone coproduct. Agent expansion using Stacks Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets, and the existing finite-list cardinal bound; HTT read online, not archived.

proof.text: It remains to bound the cones. Use the explicit join and its blockwise simplicial operators in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. In $A\star\Delta^0$, a simplex in a mixed summand $A_i\times(\Delta^0)_j$ with $i\geq0$ and $j\geq1$ is degenerate: repeat two adjacent vertices in its final block. If $j=0$ but its $A_i$ component is degenerate, it is again degenerate by repeating the corresponding vertices of the initial block. The pure $\Delta^0$ summand is degenerate in every positive degree, leaving its single vertex. A pure $A$ simplex that is degenerate remains so under the pure-factor inclusion. Consequently every nondegenerate cone simplex is among the pure nondegenerate simplices of $A$, the cone vertex, or the mixed pair $(a,*)$ with $a$ nondegenerate and final block of length one. There are therefore at most two copies of $N(A)$ and one additional element; their union has size less than $\kappa$. In particular the cone of the empty shape is exactly $\Delta^0$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.2, printed p. 433: the cardinal estimate for the successor-stage representative set S and its cone coproduct. Agent expansion using Stacks Tag 017R, lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets, and the existing finite-list cardinal bound; HTT read online, not archived.

proof.text: In a degreewise coproduct the simplicial operators preserve the summand label. By the definition of degeneracy in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], a simplex is degenerate in that coproduct exactly when it is degenerate in its own summand: a degeneracy witness must have the same label, and conversely a witness in a summand remains one in the coproduct. Hence the nondegenerate simplices are precisely the disjoint union of the summands' nondegenerate simplices. Each $A_r$ has fewer than $\lambda<\kappa$ such simplices, and Step 6 bounds each $A_r^{\triangleright}$ by $\kappa$. Since $|R|<\kappa$, regularity bounds both disjoint unions strictly below $\kappa$. By [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], both coproducts are $\kappa$-small, as required; this includes the empty coproduct.
